decisions.reason: As a low-cost extension of the established door-hardware range with no negative market signal yet, it is worth keeping on the market while demand becomes clearer.
This handle family broadens the firm's catalogue depth for architects and project customers, and with little evidence of underperformance the option value of retaining it remains positive.
Because it is close to the core business and design variants are important in this market, management would keep it until clearer evidence shows insufficient customer acceptance.
The product fits the firm's design-led fittings portfolio and likely has limited continuation cost, so abandoning it after only a short market period would be premature.
Keeping this lever-handle family preserves assortment breadth and cross-selling potential in the established business, while uncertainty about its full sales potential is still unresolved.

The electronic access system matches the firm's strategic move toward integrated digital building solutions, and its innovative positioning justifies continued market presence while adoption uncertainty resolves.
